page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6.8xlarge is a general-purpose virtual machine instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The instance provides 32 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 16 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, yielding a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage is not bundled with this instance, and it includes a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks position the ecs.g6.8xlarge in the average tier for multi-core operations and memory bandwidth. While single-core performance, such as stress-ng single-core CPU and single-threaded gzip compression, falls into the bottom 25% tier, multi-threaded workloads show better scaling. The instance achieves average-tier results in Geekbench multi-core tests, Passmark CPU and memory scores, and Redis SET operations. Memory bandwidth tests show average performance, with read-only large block speeds reaching 108.04 GB/sec and write large block speeds at 47.67 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6.8xlarge offers a balanced resource density suitable for enterprise workloads that do not require specialized GPU acceleration or high-speed local NVMe storage. Given its balanced CPU-to-memory ratio and average multi-core performance, this instance is suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, database operations, and multi-threaded software compilation.

Built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via the KVM hypervisor, this instance offers a balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. It does not include local storage, relying instead on network-attached storage, and provides a baseline network bandwidth of 10 Gbps. Benchmark results place the instance in the average tier for multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth, and database operations, though single-core performance is relatively weak. The ecs.g6.8xlarge is suited for balanced workloads such as static web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, and general-purpose database applications.
